extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, patent owners, third-party requesters, and USPTO examiners
extracted.subtask_description: MPEP guidance on procedures, requirements, limits, and expectations for requesting and conducting ex parte reexamination of issued U.S. patents (35 U.S.C. §§302-305 and related rules). Covers who may request, what constitutes a basis for ordering reexamination, timing, prior art limits, public access, amendments, and conduct expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement of a substantial new question of patentability
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office initially determines if “a substantial new question of patentability” (35 U.S.C. 303(a)) is presented. If such a new question has been presented, reexamination will be ordered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A reexamination request must present a substantial new question of patentability as the threshold for ordering reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may request reexamination / timing of request
rubrics_metrics.description: Anyone can request reexamination at any time during the period of enforceability of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reexamination requests are not limited to the patent owner; third parties may file requests while the patent remains enforceable. See related sections on persons who may file and timing (e.g., MPEP §§2212, 2211).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior art limitations in ex parte reexamination under 35 U.S.C. 304
rubrics_metrics.description: In ex parte reexaminations ordered under 35 U.S.C. 304, prior art considered during reexamination is limited to prior art patents or printed publications applied under the appropriate parts of 35 U.S.C. 102 and 103.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patents may also be applied in a double patenting rejection (see MPEP §2258 subsection I.D.). By contrast, in ex parte reexaminations ordered under 35 U.S.C. 257 (supplemental examination) the prior art considered during reexamination is not limited (see MPEP §2801).

rubrics_metrics.name: Time for decision on request and special dispatch requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Decision on a request for reexamination submitted under 35 U.S.C. 302 must be made no later than 3 months from its filing, and the remainder of the proceeding must proceed with “special dispatch” within the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similarly, a decision on a request for supplemental examination submitted under 35 U.S.C. 257 must be made no later than 3 months from its filing (see MPEP §2815), and any ex parte reexamination proceeding ordered as a result of a supplemental examination proceeding must proceed with “special dispatch.” Special dispatch requirements derive from 35 U.S.C. 305.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex parte nature of the reexamination proceeding
rubrics_metrics.description: If ordered, the actual reexamination proceeding is ex parte in nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although anyone may file a request, once reexamination is ordered the proceeding proceeds ex parte between the patent owner and the Office; third-party participation is restricted compared to inter partes procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of claim amendments cannot enlarge claim scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The scope of a claim cannot be enlarged by amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any amendment by patent owner during reexamination must not broaden the claimed scope; this is a firm limitation on allowable claim changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination proceedings normally conclude with a reexamination certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: If ordered, a reexamination proceeding will normally be conducted to its conclusion and the issuance of a reexamination certificate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When prosecution of a reexamination proceeding is terminated, a reexamination certificate is issued which indicates the status of all claims following the reexamination (see MPEP §§2287–2288).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public access to reexamination files and handling of non-patent literature
rubrics_metrics.description: All reexamination and patent files are open to the public, but the reexamination file is scanned into IFW to provide an electronic format copy; public access and copying may be made from the electronic format copy available through Patent Center.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any remaining paper files are not available to the public. Images of non-patent literature (NPL) cited in public files are not available for viewing or downloading through Patent Center. Certified copies of the full contents of the files, including NPL, are available from the Patent and Trademark Copy Fulfillment Branch and may be ordered online through the Certified Copy Center storefront.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectations on party conduct and prohibition of litigation tactics
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties are cautioned that the reexamination statute, regulations, and published examining procedures do not countenance so-called “litigation tactics” in reexamination proceedings. The parties are expected to conduct themselves accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions of papers not provided for in the reexamination regulations and/or appearing to be excluded by the regulation should be filed with an appropriate petition to accept the paper and/or waive the regulation(s), or not filed at all. Multiple submissions such as a reply and a sur-reply are not provided for. Parties are advised to adhere to 37 CFR 11.18(b) throughout the proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differences from regular examination (types of rejections, forms, and timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reexamination proceedings are very similar to regular examination procedures, but there are notable differences: certain limitations as to the kind of rejections which may be made in a reexamination ordered under 35 U.S.C. 304, special reexamination forms to be used, and time periods set to provide 'special dispatch.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners should be aware of procedural differences (including applicable forms and restricted rejection types) and consult relevant MPEP sections (e.g., scope-of-rejection guidance, forms list) when handling reexamination matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation on public availability of paper files and NPL images
rubrics_metrics.description: All public access to and copying of the reexamination file may be made from the electronic format copy available through Patent Center; any remaining paper files are not available to the public and images of NPL cited in public files are not available via Patent Center.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To obtain certified copies of full contents including NPL, requestors must use the Certified Copy Center storefront; see MPEP references for ordering certified copies.
